absent: Full C layout and initial values for apic_chip_data and vector_cleanup beyond fields observed in use.
Declaration and initialisation of vector_lock, vector_searchmask, vector_matrix and per processor vector tables.
Behaviour and error codes of the irq matrix allocator and reservation accounting.
Semantics of trace hooks, debug display helpers and diagnostic warning primitives.
Hardware effects of APIC destination calculation and vector activation helpers.
Core interrupt layer contracts for affinity masks, domain creation, descriptor lookup and activation flags.
Timer, list, NUMA mask and firmware node helpers used during selection and cleanup.
Legacy PIC probe, IOAPIC ownership bitmap and cascade exclusion rationale.

findings.text: System vector reservation, matrix bringup, legacy marking, vector domain creation and interrupt count probing are exposed for early boot. They establish allocator limits, the default domain and the usable legacy range before normal handling.

Processor online and offline transitions are exposed so arrival installs legacy descriptors and departure retires pending moves plus takes the matrix offline. These are the hotplug hooks for vector state.
Predicates recognising IOAPIC and HPET firmware specifications are exposed for domain parent matching, together with the early interrupt count probe used during initialisation.

Per interrupt chip records start cleared with an empty deferred cleanup linkage and a node hint. Release only frees the record. Bulk creation unwinds predecessors when a later member cannot be obtained.

A configuration refresh associates a vector with a destination derived from the chosen processor, marks that processor vector active, narrows visible effective affinity to that single processor and emits observation. The caller already serialises this mutation.

When a new vector is installed the prior deferred state is cleared first. Absence of a prior vector or presence of the shutdown placeholder leads directly to installation. Otherwise an online prior target causes deferral with stashed location, while an offline prior target allows immediate release.

Creation policy distinguishes managed interrupts which only reserve managed capacity, requests carrying an explicit mask which attempt immediate placement, and remaining requests which take a global reservation for later activation.

Placement first retains the current location when it remains online and acceptable. Otherwise it tries progressively wider processor sets, preferring node locality combined with affinity before falling back to affinity alone, node alone and finally all online processors.

Deactivation leaves plain fixed interrupts and globally reserved interrupts untouched, otherwise clears current and stashed vectors and restores either a global reservation or a shutdown placeholder. Freeing clears vectors, drops reservation counts, resets core data and then frees the record.

Legacy interrupts start pinned to processor zero with an architecture derived vector. If already active only the hardware description is refreshed. Otherwise the entry is made reservable, cleared and later reassigned, while the cascade position is never used.

Successful creation attaches the local APIC controller, records Linux and hardware numbers, enforces single target delivery, requires interrupt context for handling and defers affinity programming until activation. Disabled APIC or cascade legacy requests fail immediately.

Domain selection only claims IOAPIC or HPET specifications when wide APIC identifiers are not permitted. Matching requires a single parameter and either a recognised firmware node name with equal index or a compatible device description for IOAPIC.

A single vector spin lock serialises chip record mutation, matrix reservation and allocation, shared search mask use and cleanup queue changes. Outer paths disable interrupts while acquiring it and inner helpers assert it is held. Debug display copies under it then formats after release.

Each interrupt owns a record holding current vector and processor, previous vector and processor for migration, progress and mode flags for movement, managed operation and reservation state, hardware vector plus destination fields, a deferred cleanup linkage and the Linux interrupt number.

Deferred retirement uses per processor queues with a timer and a list of records awaiting release of their prior vector. Domain behaviour is collected in an operations table providing selection, allocation, release, activation, deactivation and debug display hooks.

An interrupt moves from unassigned to reserved with a shutdown placeholder, to assigned on activation, through possible affinity driven reassignments, back to cleared plus reservation or placeholder on deactivation, and finally to detached and freed on release.

A superseded vector enters a pending state with its former location remembered and remains queued until its replacement is observed. Retirement checks for lingering hardware pending state and either completes release or re arms a short delayed recheck. Offline teardown forces a non checking pass.

Allocation, release, activation, deactivation and debug display arrive through the vector domain operations. Allocation validates platform state and legacy constraints, activation chooses among direct assignment, shutdown placeholder, managed activation or reserved activation based on mode and request flags.

Affinity changes are accepted only for activated interrupts, intersect the request with online processors under lock, then follow the managed path for managed interrupts and the regular placement path otherwise, reporting success with a dedicated status.

A new placement is refused when a prior migration is still pending or the record remains queued for retirement. Allocation can also fail from capacity exhaustion, which surfaces as an error and, for reserved activation, a warning when effective affinity escapes the requested set.

Retirement may observe the old vector still pending in hardware and must defer completion with a short delay and a single warning. Offline transition warns when its timer cannot be cancelled synchronously or when the retirement queue is left non empty.

The matrix allocator is sized by total vector count with distinct lower bounds for external and system ranges. Early probing also caps total interrupts by vectors multiplied by processor count and adds per processor headroom plus extra for message signalled sources.

A dedicated managed shutdown vector serves as placeholder for reserved but unassigned interrupts. Cleared per processor slots use a shutdown sentinel and unusable legacy positions use an unused sentinel. Legacy vectors derive from Linux numbers through an architecture mapping and the cascade index stays excluded.
